tone.voice: a no-nonsense operations expert — fast answers, zero ambiguity

trust_signals: estimated time of arrival always visible
ux_norms: map is the primary UI element on most screens
ETA is always the most prominent information
status updates are real-time and clear
minimal steps to complete a booking or shipment
bulk actions for logistics management screens
notification system is critical — always active

visual_language.style: functional and fast — map dominates, everything else is secondary
photography_rules: driver profile photos only — professional and clear
vehicle photography for fleet management screens
no decorative photography on operational screens
visual_language.background_treatment: dark map backgrounds or clean light grey — never decorative
visual_language.empty_state_style: simple SVG — truck, package, or map pin with direct actionable copy
visual_language.onboarding_visual: flat vector — map, route, or vehicle theme — clean and fast-feeling
visual_language.illustration_style: when used: flat technical vector — never organic or decorative

monetization_models: per trip or per shipment fee
SaaS per seat for fleet management
compliance_notes: GDPR for location and personal data

avoid: Never show an ETA without updating it in real time
Never hide a shipment status change — push notification required for every status update
Never use estimated delivery ranges wider than 2 days without explanation
Never show a map that does not reflect the current real-time position
Never require manual refresh to see status updates — always live
Never use casual language for delays — professional and informative always
enforce: Real-time tracking always shown when available — live map is the standard
ETA always shown prominently and updated continuously
Every status change triggers a notification — no silent updates
Proof of delivery always available — photo or signature
Customer support contact always one tap away from tracking screen
Delay reason always communicated — never just a new ETA with no explanation
